answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a proof-of-unique-work bond: each agent stakes an opal-tier deposit that stays locked while it trades, and every identity must complete a distinct verifiable computation that cannot be copied across accounts. Like a gale stripping weak shelters, the bond makes mass fake identities expensive, since each one ties up real capital and compute. A raven-style random audit then samples identities, and any agent caught reusing proofs loses its stake, so forging thousands of fake agents costs far more than any fraud could return.
